items.title: Kelly Lee Owens announces two-day music festival in Wales to celebrate grassroots venues as part of Hometown Meltdown
items.summary:
Kelly Lee Owens has announced the line-up for her Hometown Meltdown festival in North Wales, celebrating the country’s grassroots venues.

The electronic musician and producer will curate and perform at Neuadd Ogwen in Bethesda on December 12 and 13, bringing together established and emerging Welsh talent for the first event in a nationwide series.

The festival is a partnership between London’s Southbank Centre and the Music Venue Trust , which aims to take the spirit of the long-running artist-curated Meltdown festival into grassroots venues across the UK.

Owens will perform on both days, with Saturday’s bill also featuring Tokomololo and Osgled. Sunday will include a DJ set from Super Furry Animals ‘ Gruff Rhys , alongside Casi, Høst and Gwenno Morgan. Find any remaining tickets here .

“My Welsh roots have always been incredibly important to me – especially placing the emphasis on the pool of creative talent and energies in the north of Wales!” Owens said in a statement.

“I’m excited to work with Hometown Meltdown to bring focus to this part of the UK!”

View this post on Instagram 

The event will also celebrate Neuadd Ogwen’s role in supporting Welsh-language music and culture, with the venue describing grassroots spaces as essential meeting places for local communities.

“Grassroots music venues are about more than just putting on gigs; they’re places where communities come together, new talent gets a platform, and people can experience live music right on their doorstep,” said the…

items.title: Maruja thank fans for supporting them through burnout after “beautiful and brutal year” with new live album ‘The Holy Inadequate’ and Ritual Union headline set

The record documents a breakthrough period for the band, who toured extensively throughout 2025, playing sold-out shows across Asia, North America, the UK, Ireland and Europe.

However, the intensity of their touring schedule eventually took its toll, forcing the four-piece to take time away from live performances.

“2025 was a beautiful and brutal year for us,” the band said in a statement accompanying the release. “We recorded and released ‘Pain To Power’ amidst playing 109 shows.”

They continued: “We are endlessly grateful to do what we love, and to the fans who continually renew us through their presence at our live shows, giving their time, bodies and hearts to connect with us and each other through the music.”

“Ecstatic highs are met with precarious lows of life on the road,” they explained. “Navigating the industry’s many challenges while living our own complex lives led us to burnout at the end of 2025.”

Today, it’s thanks to a freshly dug-up tweet from Jon Ossoff, the newly re-elected Georgia senator, who sincerely wrote in 2012: “Looking forward to your writeup of the new @imaginedragons album.”

It’s an all-timer, up there with Phoebe Bridgers saying that she thinks about the site’s review of Jet’s second album (a video of a monkey pissing in its own mouth) once a day, and Halsey wishing that the Pitchfork office, which is on the site of the 9/11 attacks in New York, would “collapse already”. items.title: Life Without Buildings reunite after 24 years and make hometown live return in Glasgow
items.summary:
Life Without Buildings have reunited and played their first public live shows in 24 years, returning to the stage for four concerts in Glasgow and London.

The cult Scottish post-punk group, who split in 2002 after releasing just one studio album, performed at Glasgow’s Saint Luke’s on Monday and Tuesday (November 16 and 17), before playing two sold-out shows at London’s KOKO on Thursday and Friday (November 19 and 20).

The reunion was originally announced in January as part of the celebrations marking the 50th anniversary of Rough Trade, before the band added their hometown dates .

The four-piece – vocalist Sue Tompkins, guitarist Robert Dallas Gray, bassist Chris Evans and drummer Will Bradley – played 14 songs at their first comeback show, including fan favourites ‘The Leanover’, ‘Juno’, ‘Young Offenders’ and ‘New Town’.

They opened with ‘Love Trinity’, a song recorded towards the end of their original career that was only officially released in 2025, before closing with ‘New Town’.

Did anyone go see Life Without Buildings this week? They were brilliant! I met a couple yesterday who had come from New York to see them. pic.twitter.com/K39bCAbjXu 

— stuart murdoch (@nee_massey) November 19, 2026

items.title: ‘I do a really good version of AC/DC’s Highway to Hell, which throws people’: Sharleen Spiteri’s honest playlist
items.summary:
The Texas singer was fascinated by Elvis Costello as a kid and admires Nancy Sinatra’s sass and strength, but which of her own songs changed her life?

The first song I fell in love with
My mum gave me an old Dansette record player and a pile of albums. I must have been eight or 10, with my younger sister Corinne, getting butterflies to These Boots Are Made for Walkin’ by Nancy Sinatra. Years later, I read that she was told to sing it with a much more provocative attitude. You can hear the sass and the strength. Maybe that’s where my whole “don’t fuck with me” thing came from.

The song I do at karaoke
Give me any Marvin Gaye song, like You’re All I Need to Get By, and I’m all over it, but I’d normally pull someone up to duet with me.

items.title: Macaulay Culkin to return in ‘Home Alone’ sequel, written by Seth Rogen
items.summary:
Macaulay Culkin is reportedly set to return as Kevin McCallister in a new Home Alone sequel, with Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg attached to write and produce the film.

READ MORE: ‘Home Alone 2: Lost In New York’ – 25 things you didn’t know about the Christmas classic 

According to Variety , the new film is in development at the Disney-owned 20th Century Studios, with Rogen and Goldberg working with Culkin to develop a screenplay based on an idea from the latter.

The pair will also produce the film through their Point Grey Pictures company, having previously collaborated on comedies including Superbad , Pineapple Express and This Is The End .

The project would see Culkin reprise his most famous role for the first time on the big screen since 1992’s Home Alone 2: Lost In New York , more than three decades after he last played the character.

No director, additional cast members or release date have been announced, and the film remains in the early stages of development.

The news comes after it was reported in July that Disney had been courting Culkin about returning to the franchise.

The actor had previously revealed his idea for a sequel , which would reverse the premise of the original films by having an adult Kevin locked out of his house by his own son. The actor suggested that Kevin could be a widower or divorcee struggling to balance work and fatherhood, leading his frustrated child to turn his father’s old tricks against him.

Meanwhile, the director of the first two Home Alone films, Chris Columbus, has expressed doubts about the possibility of a sequel…

items.title: Britney Spears Apologizes to Her Family on Instagram: ‘I Just Miss Them Like Crazy’
items.summary:
Britney Spears posted a public apology to her family on Saturday (Nov. 21), writing on Instagram that she regretted revisiting past conflicts in public.

“I’m so very sorry for bringing up past issues, but I think I did because I realized I needed to protect my heart,” Spears wrote. “It’s the way I love, and when I love you, I really love you.”

She described her own conduct as “childish and embarrassing,” adding: “Thoughts on the past, I’m obviously human, and there actually might be something to those things I said psychology-wise; either way, I’m sorry to my family for bringing up those memories.”

Spears said the conversation had never taken place directly. “I’ve never actually spoken to them face to face on it,” she wrote. “I just miss them like crazy! And I’m very sorry!” She also called herself “blessed to have such a beautiful family.”

Spears is the eldest child of Jamie and Lynne Spears, who are divorced. She has a brother, Bryan, and a sister, Jamie Lynn Spears .

The relationship has been publicly strained for years. Spears spent 13 years under a conservatorship, established in February 2008 with her father as conservator, which gave others control over her finances, career and personal decisions. After an explosive court hearing in June 2021 in which she testified against the arrangement, a Los Angeles judge suspended Jamie Spears that September and terminated the conservatorship on Nov. 12, 2021.

In the years since, Spears has repeatedly addressed the fallout. “Honestly my family embarrassed me and hurt me deeply,” she wrote in December 2021, a month after…
items.t: Britney Spears Apologizes to Her Family on Instagram: ‘I Just Miss Them Like Crazy’

items.title: Miley Cyrus Marries Maxx Morando in Poolside Ceremony Led by the Flaming Lips’ Wayne Coyne
items.summary:
Miley Cyrus married Maxx Morando on Saturday (Nov. 21) in a poolside ceremony in Palm Springs, Calif., with the Flaming Lips ’ Wayne Coyne officiating, one month after the couple sang “Let’s Get Married” together on the Hollywood Bowl stage.

Coyne, who worked with Cyrus on her 2015 album Miley Cyrus & Her Dead Petz and joined her onstage at the Hollywood Bowl in October, led the vows as Cyrus, 33, and Morando, 28, stood beneath an arch of white flowers in front of family and friends, according to photos published by People . Cyrus wore a long-sleeved white satin gown with a high neck, open back and small train, and was photographed wiping away tears during the vows, while Morando wore a black suit.

Among the guests were her mother, Tish Cyrus, and husband Dominic Purcell; her sister Noah Cyrus ; and her father, Billy Ray Cyrus , along with Elizabeth Hurley. The celebrations began the night before with a rehearsal dinner, glimpsed in Instagram photos posted by Cyrus’ stepsister Lily-Rose Purcell that showed tables dressed with dark red flowers and small candles, and a menu topped with an “M+M” monogram.

The wedding caps a year in which the relationship moved from the edges of Cyrus’ public life to the center of her work. “Let’s Get Married,” which Morando co-wrote and co-produced, appears on Bass Persuades , her 10th studio album and her first released simply as Miley. Its black-and-white video, directed by Mert Alas and shot at West Hollywood’s Chateau Marmont, casts Morando opposite her — a dress rehearsal, as it turned out, for the real thing two months later.

items.t: Miley Cyrus Marries Maxx Morando in Palm Springs

The band delivered an emotional set packed with hits and gave a special shoutout to Mexico and its president. The British collective also brought out veteran guitarist Johnny Marr and Argentine rapper Trueno as special guests.

“I f— with Mexico because you have a revolutionary spirit here,” Gorillaz frontman Damon Albarn told the crowd. “This is an inspirational country.”

The first day of the festival’s 16th edition featured established acts and rising artists across indie, soul, electro-pop, folk and contemporary rap. Female artists — performing solo or with their bands — were especially well represented, including CHVRCHES, Violet Grohl, Olivia Dean, CMAT, Grace Ives, Anna Luna and Darianna Everett.

Gorillaz Celebrate Mexico’s ‘Revolutionary Spirit’ at Corona Capital, Bring Out Johnny Marr and Trueno

Gorillaz returned to Mexico City on Friday (Nov. 20) for the first time in eight years, headlining the opening day of Corona Capital. During the long-awaited show, frontman Damon Albarn praised the country’s “revolutionary spirit.” Guitarist Johnny Marr and Argentine rapper Trueno joined the band as special guests — and Albarn also gave a shoutout to Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum.

Last week, Sheinbaum traveled to Shenzhen, China, for the 2026 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, flying economy alongside other passengers. The decision made waves on Chinese social media — and came up again Friday at the popular Mexican festival, where 72,000 people packed the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, according to promoter Ocesa.

“I f— with Mexico because you have a revolutionary spirit here,” Albarn told the crowd. “This is an inspirational country, and I don’t know too much about your president, but the fact that she traveled economy class, for me, is a really important… It’s a statement, you know? So, I salute you all.”

Albarn made the comment while wearing a red beret and military-style jacket, an image that fit the occasion: Mexico’s Revolution Day, observed every Nov. 20 to mark the start of the 1910 armed uprising against Porfirio Díaz, who had been in power for more than 30 years.

Trueno and Gorillaz’s Damon Albarn perform at Corona Capital on Friday (Nov. 20). Credit: Liliana Estrada

Manchester-based Megatone Sound Foundation and Baron Turbo Charge have rejuvenated the culture to offer a sense of belonging and empowerment

For a generation of young Black Mancunians, some of the history lessons that mattered most were not taught in classrooms, but through towering stacks of amps and speakers, turntables and Jamaican records.

“We didn’t know where we fit in. We didn’t know our history. Our parents were busy working two or three jobs,” says Errol “Barzy” Beaumont, a founder member of Baron Turbo Charge, Manchester’s long-running reggae sound system. “It was the records – Burning Spear, Bob Marley, Culture, that were telling us about our culture, which wasn’t on the school curriculum. For us, the sound system was not just entertainment – it was an education.”

items.title: Fontaines DC review – thrilling gothic grandeur from a band vaulting into greatness
items.summary:
M&S Bank Arena, Liverpool
Just a few years since playing little dive bars, the Irish rockers have confidently scaled up to huge rooms like this – and are now one of the key interpreters of modern malaise

A mere seven years since their debut, Dogrel, Fontaines DC have enjoyed a virtually seamless passage from Dublin dive bars to arenas, with stadiums to follow next year. Each step has been taken seemingly effortlessly in their stride and this latest outing is no exception. Bathed in shimmering blue light, the band are well into hymnal opener Six Shot Morning before we even see sight of singer Grian Chatten. He wanders on while singing, an entrance worthy of Frank Sinatra.

Chatten has previously seemed to distrust showbiz, but if anything the singer seems far more comfortable on the bigger stage than he ever did on smaller ones. With his Korn T-shirt, unfeasibly baggy trousers and tiny tattoo reading “deadly” in capitals, he leaps around, raises his arms to whip up the crowd and points the microphone towards them to sing key lines. Similarly, music this intense, dark, elegiac and even bleak – which speaks to the void at the heart of much modern life – is hardly typical arena fare but works brilliantly by taking on a more anthemic, celebratory aspect. It’s certainly weirdly thrilling hearing Chatten’s lines such as “We’re all depressed, running on a wheel” or “I don’t feel anything in the modern world” – or a song as plainly dark as Jackie Down the Line – become enormous, arena-uniting sing-songs.
items.t: Fontaines DC review – thrilling gothic grandeur from a band vaulting into greatness

Isaac Eiger’s solo venture leaves jangle pop behind for a wilder sound. Often it owes a debt to Alex G, but what indie-rock song doesn’t these days?

From New York via Montana
Recommended if you like Cameron Winter, Tobias Jesso Jr, Alex G
Up next Supporting Caroline on tour in Canada and the US until 19 November

Isaac Eiger is something of a scene legend in the world of American indie-rock. Raised in Bozeman, Montana, he was the founder and lead singer of the cult shoegaze-adjacent six-piece Strange Ranger, who left heartbroken a small, fervent fanbase when they announced their breakup in 2023. Taking a discernibly British approach to their sound, Strange Ranger traversed C86-y jangle-pop before landing on Madchester rave-up for their final album, 2023’s Pure Music. But Eiger is nothing if not musically worldly: he has written and produced with both underground heroes (Cassandra Jenkins, Chanel Beads) and nascent pop stars (Adéla, Frost Children).

Ever-prolific, Eiger also has a solo project under the name Threshold, with which he released a gauzy, 19-minute EP in 2024 called Thief. Earlier this year, he released Stillwater, the first single from the debut Threshold album, due for release in 2027 on the London-based label Untitled. Although Stillwater has some clear influences – it owes some phrasings and intonations to Alex G, but what indie-rock song doesn’t these days? – it’s still a remarkable song: expansive and…

items.title: The month’s best experimental album: Stella Z’s ambient adventures into lucid dreaming
items.summary:
(CDR)
Based around sounds recorded on her trips back to China, the Fujian-born, London-based producer creates a curious nocturnal collage on Thunder Is the Sky Dreaming

Lucid dreaming is one of the influences behind Thunder Is the Sky Dreaming, the new record from Fujian-born, London-based producer Stella Z. “Every night is an adventure,” she writes in the liner notes, “I can even smell things in certain dreams.” The eight tracks here are suitably sensory, scattered with effervescent sounds, ephemeral whispers and polyrhythmic percussion.

Many of the sounds and textures were recorded during trips back to China – the ambient noises of a pharmacy or the Fujian mountains late at night – a curious, collage-like approach that underpins the record. On The Somnium Is Awaiting My Cue, we hear what appear to be insects buzzing around a plodding bassline and sporadic woodwind motifs, while electronics softly spiral. Similarly hypnotic is Mira Miruna, on which the echoes of words gradually reveal themselves among the fizzing, softly discordant arrangement: a warped, increasingly urgent call to “wake up”, reminiscent of the foggy state as you rise from sleep. Z amplifies this heady feeling later on in Exit, Elsewhere, where her overlapping narration and rattling bells cause total disorientation.

Continue reading...

items.title: ‘We’re the most arrogant of all apes!’ A delightfully mind-expanding encounter with Peter Gabriel
items.summary:
From sampling to streaming, the rock legend has always been in thrall to technology – but is superintelligence a step too far? Back with an epic new album, he unpacks his remarkable ideas

Peter Gabriel asks me to fetch my laptop: he wants to show me a video of himself playing a keyboard duet with a bonobo called Kanzi. In fairness, said footage is, as Gabriel suggests, “extraordinary”. Working with primatologist Sue Savage-Rumbaugh, who developed a means of communicating with bonobos involving sign language and a speech-synthesis keyboard, Gabriel plays droning chords on a synthesiser while Kanzi picks out complementary notes on a piano. “Look, she likes that note, which is a ninth, and then she finds the octave,” he enthuses as the video plays. “There’s a real musicality there.”

It is all deeply unlikely, but it seems the perfect illustration of how easily a conversation with Gabriel can go wildly – if fascinatingly – off-piste. I’ve only been in his company for 10 minutes, long enough to ask a solitary question about his epic new album o\i: its 13 tracks last nearly 90 minutes, the result, he suggests, of a longstanding interest in African music “which made me realise that a song could last as long as a song could last”, and of “being old enough to think ‘fuck it’, really”. For anyone who feels that an hour and a half of exquisitely arranged, beautifully produced, occasionally deeply strange art rock – its sound shapeshifting from the folk-flecked A Hard Lesson to the glowing pop hues of Till Your Mind Is Shining – is too meagre an offering, it arrives in…
items.t: ‘We will become cyborgs!’ Peter Gabriel on bonobo ape duets, building a Jurassic Park for plants – and why AI will make great music
